doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: St. Louis trumpeters: Bross Woods, Baby James, Louis Metcalf
summary: Brower runs through a list of St. Louis trumpeters and Terry gives his recollections.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: We talked about a lot of – we talked about a number of St. Louis trumpet players, and I have a long list. I just want to go through them, and if you have a recollection or any thought about any of these people, maybe you could offer it. Bross Woods.

Bross Woods was a very, very simple type of player. Played very, very melodic and very lightly. Nothing powerful. He didn’t play real high, didn’t play real loud. Just played sort of in the groove. He was a very jovial person. Real nice cat. Everyone loved Bross. Bross Woods. I don’t even remember what his first real name was, but he was a Woods, and we all – everybody called him Bross Woods.
Was he your senior? A contemporary?
Oh yeah, much older than me. I was probably the youngest one on the scene in those days, among the trumpet players.
Baby James. Baby James was a little bit before my time. I – he’s just like a hearsay player. I didn’t – I never really knew Baby James, but . . .
Louis Metcalf was an old-timer who was a follower of Louis Armstrong. He went to Canada and became ensconced in the Canadian scene up there and was on the scene for a long, long time
I don’t remember that name. Ed Allen. Maybe I misquoted a name or you misunderstood.
